_doc: HMTc Category 33 (Chocolate, Cocoa and Confectionery) compiler config. Method v2.0 (government-limit default). Every cell names EXPLICIT register ids (a LOOKUP, not a computation); occurrence never selects a number. High public/litigation salience (cocoa-Cd scrutiny + imported-candy lead), so every published value cites the STRICTEST applicable sovereign per product form and the legislated product-form splits are preserved as form_splits (never collapsed to one number, because certifying dark chocolate against a milk-chocolate ceiling would be indefensible). Cadmium: EU Reg. 2023/915 gives the most GRANULAR cocoa-solids split, but it is NOT the strictest for high-cocoa product — MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 + Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019 cap Cd at 300 ug/kg for all >=40% cocoa (dark chocolate and cocoa powder bind 300, not EU's 800/600) and 200 for <40% cocoa; EU 100 wins only the very-low-cocoa milk-chocolate bin; FSANZ/Singapore/Israel 500 corroborate (looser). The Cd form is therefore strictest-sovereign-per-form (100/200/300), not the EU values. Nickel: EU Reg. 2024/1987 by cocoa-solids split (2500/7000/15000), the only jurisdiction that sets it. Lead and total-arsenic in chocolate are unregulated by EU/Codex/FDA; the strictest binding sovereign is MERCOSUR GMC 12/2011 (Paraguay concurs), split by cocoa content (<40% 200 / >=40% 400). Confectionery lead binds the MERCOSUR/Paraguay binding candy ML (100) with FDA 2006 candy guidance (0.1 ppm) as US concurrence. Colour-additive purity specs (21 CFR 73.x 'Caramel; food use' etc.) are NOT candy MLs and are excluded by the engine. Panel: 8 totals (Pb, Cd, tAs, tHg, Ni, Sn, Al, total Cr) + species controls (iAs, Cr-VI); MeHg is not-material (no marine-bioaccumulation pathway in a dry confection). See docs/governance for the Cat-7-dissolution Step-0 event that created Cat 33.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default; explicit-id lookup; legislated product-form splits preserved)

chocolate.name: Cocoa and chocolate products (cocoa powder, dark, milk, chips)
chocolate.native_basis_label: product as placed on the market (as-sold solid)

form_split.instrument: MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 (Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay); Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019 concurs. EU 2023/915, Codex and FDA set no lead ML for chocolate/cocoa, so the strictest binding sovereign limit governs; it splits by cocoa content.

forms.form: chocolate and cocoa products with <40% cocoa (e.g., milk chocolate)
chocolate and cocoa products with >=40% cocoa (e.g., dark chocolate, chips, cocoa powder)

form_split.instrument: Strictest applicable sovereign cadmium limit per product form. EU Reg. 2023/915 provides the most GRANULAR cocoa-solids split (milk <30% = 100, <50% = 300, >=50% = 800, cocoa powder = 600), but it is NOT the strictest for high-cocoa product: MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019 cap cadmium at 300 ug/kg for ALL chocolate/cocoa >=40% cocoa (so dark chocolate and cocoa powder bind 300, not EU's 800/600), and at 200 for <40% cocoa. FSANZ Sch 19 / Singapore / Israel set a flat 500 (looser, corroborating). EU's 100 remains the strictest for the very-low-cocoa milk-chocolate bin. Certification applies the form matching the product's declared cocoa content. This is the category's flagship, most litigation-exposed cell; it binds the strictest sovereign, which is MERCOSUR/PY 300 for the high-cocoa forms.

forms.form: milk chocolate with <30% total dry cocoa solids
chocolate and cocoa products with <40% cocoa (and >=30% total dry cocoa solids)
chocolate and cocoa products with >=40% cocoa (dark chocolate, chips, cocoa powder, cocoa paste)

form_split.instrument: MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011; Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019 concurs. Total arsenic; no EU/Codex/FDA chocolate arsenic ML, so the strictest binding sovereign limit governs, split by cocoa content.

forms.form: chocolate and cocoa products with <40% cocoa
chocolate and cocoa products with >=40% cocoa (incl. cocoa powder/paste)

control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets an inorganic-arsenic maximum level for cocoa or chocolate (inorganic arsenic is a dietary speciation defined for rice and drinking water); cocoa arsenic is regulated as total arsenic, which arithmetically bounds the inorganic fraction (iAs <= tAs). The FDA Total Diet Study (fda-tds-elements-2018-2020), routed to this row, reports a measurable inorganic-arsenic trace in chocolate, so the fraction is screened via reflex speciation on the total-As result rather than dismissed as absent.
control.reference_method: Reflex inorganic-As speciation on the total-As result; bounded by the tAs cell. No sovereign iAs ML for cocoa/chocolate.
control.trigger: reflex iAs speciation when total arsenic approaches the tAs ceiling

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury is a marine-bioaccumulation speciation with no formation pathway in a terrestrial cocoa or chocolate matrix, and it is arithmetically bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg). Every applicable mercury limit is set on total mercury, which the tHg standard caps, bounding any organomercury fraction.
not_material.regulatory_basis: Bounded by the total-Hg standard (Vietnam QCVN 8-2:2011, 50 ug/kg); no methylmercury ML for cocoa/chocolate anywhere

form_split.instrument: EU Reg. 2024/1987 (nickel maximum levels; applies from 2025-07-01), set by total dry cocoa-solids content — the same product-form split the EU uses for cadmium. No other jurisdiction sets a nickel ML for chocolate/cocoa.

forms.form: milk chocolate with <30% total dry cocoa solids
milk chocolate with >=30% total dry cocoa solids, and chocolate
cocoa powder / fat-reduced cocoa powder (drinking chocolate)

not_material.rationale: Inorganic tin migrates from tinplate cans; chocolate, cocoa powder and chips are sold in wrappers/boxes/pouches, not tinplate cans, so there is no tin source or migration route. Tin is material only for tin-plated canned product.
not_material.reference_method: Packaging control (non-tinplate); periodic ICP-MS tin verification.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No tin ML for non-canned chocolate/cocoa; the 250 mg/kg canned-food tin limit applies only to tin-plated cans

not_material.rationale: Cocoa is a natural aluminium accumulator (aluminium is taken up from soil into the cocoa bean); the aluminium present is background, not contamination. No credible regulator sets an aluminium contaminant maximum level for cocoa or chocolate; dietary aluminium is managed by intake against the EFSA TWI (1 mg/kg bw/week) and JECFA PTWI (2 mg/kg bw/week), not by a per-food ML. Matches the existing chocolate/Al determination in standards-not-material.csv.
not_material.reference_method: Aluminium managed by intake vs TWI; periodic screen; no per-food contaminant ML.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No Al contaminant ML for cocoa/chocolate in any credible jurisdiction; managed by TWI
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915 (lists no Al); Codex; FSANZ; JECFA/EFSA TWI

control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a total-chromium contaminant maximum level for any food (chromium(III) is an essential nutrient; only hexavalent chromium in drinking water is regulated). Cocoa takes up trace chromium from soil. Total chromium is screened as the substrate for the reflex Cr-VI speciation, but there is no sovereign number to align to.
control.reference_method: Total-chromium screen (ICP-MS); substrate for reflex Cr-VI speciation.
control.trigger: reflex Cr-VI speciation only if total chromium is anomalously elevated

control.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is reduced to chromium(III) in reducing, organic-rich, mildly acidic food matrices such as cocoa, and no jurisdiction sets a Cr-VI food maximum level (Cr-VI limits exist only for drinking water). Sources routed to this row (amjad2021-lahore-chocolates-metals, fda-tds-elements-2018-2020) report measurable TOTAL chromium in chocolate, so the hexavalent fraction is screened by reflex speciation on an elevated total-Cr result rather than dismissed.
control.reference_method: Reflex Cr-VI speciation on an anomalously elevated total-chromium screen; no sovereign Cr-VI food ML.
control.trigger: reflex Cr-VI speciation only if the total-chromium screen is anomalously elevated

chocolate.scope_note: Covers cocoa powder, dark chocolate, milk chocolate and chocolate chips. Cocoa sold as a beverage/drink mix routes to Cat 5 Beverages; cocoa butter (a fat) routes to Cat 30 Culinary Oils & Fats. A confection with a Supplement Facts panel routes to Cat 16. Products marketed for ages 0-5 route to Cat 1. Cadmium is a strictest-sovereign-per-form split (EU 100 for low-cocoa milk chocolate; MERCOSUR/Paraguay 200 for <40% cocoa and 300 for >=40% cocoa, which govern dark chocolate and cocoa powder below the looser EU 800/600); nickel is the EU 2024/1987 cocoa-solids split; lead and total arsenic are the MERCOSUR/Paraguay cocoa-content split. Certification applies the form matching the product's declared cocoa content.

confectionery-candy.name: Candy and confectionery (hard candy, caramels, imported/ethnic sweets)
confectionery-candy.native_basis_label: confection as placed on the market (as-sold solid)

Pb.basis_label: candy as sold (binding candy ML; FDA 2006 candy guidance concurs at 0.1 ppm as US backstop)

not_material.rationale: Sugar confectionery (hard candy, caramels, chews) has no cadmium source or migration route: there is no cocoa and no soil-uptake plant tissue at the confection level. The documented cadmium contamination platform for this category is cocoa (certified under the chocolate row, which carries the EU cocoa-solids cadmium form_split). The known imported/ethnic-candy adulteration hazard is lead (and to a lesser extent arsenic), not cadmium. Rebuttable: if a routed source reports cadmium measured in a non-cocoa confection, re-adjudicate.
not_material.reference_method: Ingredient screen; cocoa-based confections route to the chocolate row.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No candy cadmium ML in any jurisdiction; cadmium pathway is cocoa (routed to chocolate)
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915; Codex; FDA; MERCOSUR; Singapore; Paraguay

not_material.rationale: No jurisdiction sets an inorganic-arsenic maximum level for candy; the total-arsenic candy limit (MERCOSUR/Paraguay, 100 ug/kg) bounds the inorganic fraction (iAs <= tAs).
not_material.reference_method: Total-arsenic screen; no reflex inorganic-As speciation for candy.
not_material.regulatory_basis: Bounded by the total-As candy standard (100 ug/kg); no inorganic-As candy ML anywhere

not_material.rationale: Sugar, glucose syrup and confectionery fats carry no mercury source, and there is no bioaccumulation or migration pathway in a candy. The 21 CFR 73.85 'Caramel; food use' mercury figure (100 ug/kg) is a purity specification for the caramel COLOUR ADDITIVE, not a limit for caramel candy, and is not applied here. Rebuttable if a routed source reports mercury in confectionery.
not_material.reference_method: No mercury pathway; screen on any novel ingredient.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No candy mercury ML anywhere; 21 CFR 73.85 is a colour-additive purity spec, not a food ML
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU; Codex; FDA (21 CFR 73 excluded as additive-purity); MERCOSUR

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury is the organomercury speciation of mercury and is arithmetically bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg); sugar confectionery carries no mercury source and no methylmercury formation pathway, so any organomercury fraction sits below the total-mercury determination.
not_material.reference_method: Total-mercury screen; MeHg bounded by tHg.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No methylmercury candy ML anywhere; bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg)

control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a nickel maximum level for candy. A minor nickel pathway exists only where a confection contains hydrogenated fat (nickel is the hydrogenation catalyst); plain sugar/glucose confections carry none. Screened rather than dismissed so a hydrogenated-fat confection is caught.
control.reference_method: Nickel screen on any hydrogenated-fat-containing confection; no sovereign candy ML.
control.trigger: flag if the confection contains hydrogenated/partially-hydrogenated fat

not_material.rationale: No tin source in wrapped/boxed sugar confectionery; tin is a tinplate-can migration pathway only.
not_material.reference_method: Packaging control (non-tinplate); periodic ICP-MS tin verification.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No candy tin ML for non-canned product; canned-food 250 mg/kg limit applies to cans only

not_material.rationale: Aluminium in confectionery derives from the permitted additive aluminium (aluminium-lake colour, EU E173 / US 21 CFR 73), not contamination, and is managed by additive law and by intake against the EFSA/JECFA TWI, not by a per-food contaminant maximum level. No credible regulator sets an aluminium contaminant ML for candy.
not_material.reference_method: Managed by additive law + TWI; periodic screen.
not_material.regulatory_basis: Al managed by additive law (aluminium lakes) + TWI; no candy contaminant ML
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU 1333/2008; FDA 21 CFR 73/74; Codex; JECFA/EFSA TWI

control.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a total-chromium food maximum level (chromium(III) is an essential nutrient). Screened as the substrate for reflex Cr-VI speciation.
control.reference_method: Total-chromium screen; substrate for reflex Cr-VI speciation.
control.trigger: reflex Cr-VI speciation only if total chromium is anomalously elevated

not_material.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is the Cr(VI) speciation of chromium and is bounded by the total-chromium control (Cr-VI <= total Cr), which is screened for this category; no jurisdiction sets a Cr-VI food maximum level. Corroborating: Cr(VI) is reduced to chromium(III) in the reducing, sugar-rich confection matrix and does not persist as Cr(VI).
not_material.reference_method: Bounded by the total-chromium screen; no routine Cr-VI speciation, reflex only on anomalously elevated total chromium.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No Cr-VI food ML anywhere; bounded by total chromium (Cr-VI <= total Cr)

confectionery-candy.scope_note: Covers hard candy, caramels, and imported/ethnic sweets (tamarind, chili, and similar). The dominant certifiable hazard is lead (adulteration + packaging + imported ethnic sweets), which binds the FDA 2006 candy guidance (0.1 ppm) with MERCOSUR/Paraguay concurrence at 100; total arsenic is likewise a real candy limit. Cocoa-containing confections route to the chocolate row. A confection with a Supplement Facts panel (e.g., supplement gummies) routes to Cat 16.

gummies-jellies.name: Gummies and jelly sweets
gummies-jellies.native_basis_label: confection as placed on the market (as-sold solid)

Pb.basis_label: confection as sold (gummies are soft candies)

not_material.rationale: Gelatin/pectin/sugar gummies and fruit-jelly sweets have no cadmium source or migration route; there is no cocoa and no soil-uptake plant tissue at the confection level. Rebuttable if a routed source reports cadmium in a jelly confection.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No gummy/jelly-sweet cadmium ML in any jurisdiction

tAs.basis_label: confection as sold (gummies are soft candies)

not_material.rationale: No inorganic-arsenic ML for gummies/jelly sweets; the total-arsenic candy limit (100 ug/kg) bounds the inorganic fraction.
not_material.regulatory_basis: Bounded by the total-As candy standard; no inorganic-As ML anywhere

not_material.rationale: No mercury source and no bioaccumulation or migration pathway in a sugar/gelatin/pectin confection.
not_material.reference_method: No mercury pathway; screen on any novel ingredient.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No gummy/jelly mercury ML anywhere; no pathway

not_material.rationale: Methylmercury is the organomercury speciation of mercury and is arithmetically bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg); a gummy/jelly sweet carries no mercury source and no methylmercury formation pathway, so any organomercury fraction sits below the total-mercury determination.
not_material.reference_method: Total-mercury screen; MeHg bounded by tHg.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No methylmercury ML anywhere; bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg)

not_material.rationale: Gelatin/pectin/sugar gummies and fruit jellies contain no hydrogenated fat and no nickel source or migration route; no jurisdiction sets a nickel ML for confectionery. Rebuttable if a routed source reports nickel in a jelly confection.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No gummy/jelly nickel ML anywhere; no nickel pathway

not_material.rationale: No tin source in a pouched/wrapped gummy or jelly sweet; the jams/jellies tin limit (250 mg/kg) is a tinplate-can migration limit for canned product, not applicable to non-canned confection.
not_material.reference_method: Packaging control (non-tinplate); periodic ICP-MS tin verification.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No non-canned gummy/jelly tin ML; canned-jelly 250 mg/kg limit is can-only
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: Codex CXS 193; Thailand MOPH 414; EU; FDA

not_material.rationale: Aluminium in gummies derives from the permitted additive aluminium (aluminium-lake colour, EU E173 / US 21 CFR 73), managed by additive law and intake vs the TWI, not by a per-food contaminant ML.
not_material.reference_method: Managed by additive law + TWI; periodic screen.
not_material.regulatory_basis: Al managed by additive law + TWI; no gummy/jelly contaminant ML

control.rationale: No total-chromium food ML in any jurisdiction. Screened as the substrate for reflex Cr-VI speciation.
control.reference_method: Total-chromium screen; substrate for reflex Cr-VI speciation.
control.trigger: reflex Cr-VI speciation only if total chromium is anomalously elevated

not_material.rationale: Hexavalent chromium is the Cr(VI) speciation of chromium and is bounded by the total-chromium control (Cr-VI <= total Cr), which is screened for this category; no Cr-VI food maximum level exists. Corroborating: Cr(VI) reduces to chromium(III) in the reducing sugar/gelatin confection matrix and does not persist as Cr(VI).
not_material.reference_method: Bounded by the total-chromium screen; no routine Cr-VI speciation, reflex only on anomalously elevated total chromium.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No Cr-VI food ML anywhere; bounded by total chromium (Cr-VI <= total Cr)

gummies-jellies.scope_note: Covers gummies (gelatin/pectin soft candies) and jelly sweets (fruit jellies, Turkish delight). Gummies are soft candies, so the lead and total-arsenic cells bind the candy limits (100 ug/kg); fruit-jelly-sweet limits (fruit/vegetable sweets, jams/jellies) are looser and noted in the audit. Supplement gummies with a Supplement Facts panel route to Cat 16.
